audit_findings.title: Convertible-note dilution mixes incompatible equity claims
audit_findings.magnitude: 8.609 million shares; removing them raises base value from $34.25 to approximately $38.91 per share, a $4.66 or 13.6% increase
audit_findings.mechanism: The fully diluted share denominator assumes full conversion while owner earnings retains note interest and the bridge treats the $747.5 million principal as debt; this mismatches the numerator and denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: Upon conversion, the Company will (1) pay cash up to the aggregate principal amount of the Convertible Notes to be converted and (2) pay or deliver, as the case may be, cash, shares of its common stock, or a combination of cash and shares of our common stock, at the Company’s election, in respect of the remainder, if any, of its conversion obligation in excess of the aggregate principal amount of the Convertible Notes being converted.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated modeling error. However, even removing all 8.609 million conversion shares raises the bull value only from $39.22 to approximately $44.55 per share, still about 50% below the $89.60 market price. It therefore does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun a coherent debt-state case excluding full-conversion shares, then separately test a conversion case with principal cash settlement, after-tax interest add-back, incremental excess-value shares, and the capped-call offset.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition-fed growth may omit the cash cost required to reproduce it
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (filed acquisition cash outflows were $599.5 million in 2023-2025; the 2026 View Point acquisition added $93.0 million of cash consideration and $47.2 million of deferred consideration)
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquired earnings enter the historical owner-earnings trend and forecast growth, while acquisition payments are investing or financing cash flows outside owner earnings; future acquisition-dependent growth would therefore be capitalized without its required reinvestment.
audit_findings.evidence: We have completed a series of strategic acquisitions and transactions in recent years, some of which have been significant, such as the acquisitions of assets or businesses from each of the following companies: AngioDynamics, Inc. on June 8, 2023; EndoGastric Solutions, Inc. on July 1, 2024; Cook Medical Holdings, LLC on November 1, 2024; Biolife, L.L.C. on May 20, 2025; and Pentax of America, Inc. on November 3, 2025 (collectively, the “Recent Acquisitions”).
audit_findings.explanation: The acquisition contribution to reported growth is demonstrated, but the record does not separate organic owner earnings from acquired owner earnings. Acquisition spending is large relative to the $2.462 billion base equity value, so an omitted recurring acquisition requirement is reasonably capable of materially reducing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Build an acquisition-adjusted owner-earnings series, identify organic growth by year, and rerun the 3% and 6% cases using either supportable organic growth or an explicit normalized acquisition-reinvestment charge.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter misses a completed 2026 divestiture
audit_findings.magnitude: $28.0 million sale price, comprising $25.5 million received and a $2.5 million holdback; disposed owner earnings and transition economics are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor retains historical DualCap earnings while the June 2026 cash bridge reflects the sale proceeds, creating potential double counting; manufacturing and transition arrangements may also produce costs or retained earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: On January 31, 2026, Merit and Health Line International Corporation (“HL”) entered into an Asset Purchase Agreement (the “HL Purchase Agreement”), pursuant to which Merit agreed to sell certain assets relating to the Dual Cap® product line to HL for a purchase price of $ 28 million(the “Purchase Price” and such transaction, the “HL Transaction”).
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter omission and receipt of $25.5 million are demonstrated. The transaction price is only about 1.1% of base equity value, but the filing does not disclose the product line's owner earnings or the economics of the up-to-24-month transition arrangements, so the total valuation effect cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Remove DualCap's normalized owner earnings from the anchor, retain only net realizable proceeds including the holdback, quantify transition-service margins and obligations, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration may be an omitted senior cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $48.585 million, comprising $47.2 million of View Point deferred acquisition consideration and $1.385 million of contingent-consideration liabilities; approximately $0.68 per share or 2.0% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Unpaid acquisition-date consideration is a senior cash claim outside operating cash flow and owner earnings and should be deducted in the bridge unless already reflected elsewhere.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash payments related to the settlement of the contingent consideration liability recognized at fair value as of the applicable acquisition date have been reflected as a cash outflow from financing activities in the accompanying consolidated statements of cash flows.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated. Deducting the disclosed claims would reduce base value from $34.25 to approximately $33.57 per share, leaving it far below the $89.60 market price and therefore not changing the valuation conclusion. The acquired View Point business must also be included in a coherent perimeter rerun.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $47.2 million deferred View Point consideration and $1.385 million contingent-consideration balance by maturity, deduct unpaid acquisition-date obligations, avoid duplicating fair-value-change expenses, and include the corresponding acquired-business owner earnings.

audit_findings.title: Not all bridge cash is freely distributable
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum $17.493 million of China cash included in bridge cash, approximately $0.24 per share or 0.7% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any trapped cash, transfer cost, withholding tax, or delay discount reduces the cash added through the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash held by our subsidiary in China is subject to local laws and regulations that require government approval for the transfer of such funds to entities located outside of China.
audit_findings.explanation: At June 2026, China held $19.7 million of cash including restricted cash, while the $448.699 million bridge cash excludes the separately reported $2.207 million of restricted cash. Even excluding the remaining $17.493 million entirely would reduce base value by only about $0.24 per share and would not change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the exact unrestricted Chinese cash included in the bridge and apply documented withholding, approval-delay, or transfer-cost adjustments rather than automatically excluding the full balance.

audit_findings.title: Private-company stakes may not support the bridge value
audit_findings.magnitude: $27.9 million, approximately $0.39 per share or 1.1% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A realizability discount reduces the stakes bridge addition, while any investee earnings retained in owner earnings would need to be purged before the investments are added separately.
audit_findings.evidence: Investments not accounted for under the equity method of accounting are accounted for at cost minus impairment, if applicable, plus or minus changes in valuation resulting from observable transactions for identical or similar investments.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting basis does not demonstrate realizable value, so the valuation support remains unresolved. Nevertheless, writing the entire $27.9 million balance to zero would reduce base value only from $34.25 to approximately $33.86 per share, still far below the $89.60 market price. The filed record also describes historical equity-method adjustments as immaterial.
audit_findings.action: Map each investment, obtain current transaction or valuation evidence and liquidity terms, apply any warranted discount, and reconcile investee income or losses against the owner-earnings numerator.
